```{r}
library(MaMaMIA)
```

# Overview

MaMaMIA detects interspecific introgression from coverage breadth and read
counts. It is ploidy-aware: a donor and a recipient may each contribute any
number of subgenomes, and homoeologs are compared within chromosome groups.

The pipeline is:

```
preflightBams()
  -> makeAnalysisWindows()          group-aware exact-N windows
  -> extractWindowGc()              gcrank
  -> countWindowMetrics()           counts + covered bases in one htslib pass
  -> buildWindowMetrics()           breadth, lambdas
  -> scoreIntrogression()           paired donor/recipient log-ratio
  -> buildWindowMask()              panel / cohort / blacklist / physical
  -> segmentScores()                CBS + gap merging
  -> calibrateSegments()            length-stratified empirical null
  -> classifyCalls()                substitution / addition / other
```

This release is not backward compatible with version 0.99. The configuration
schema, the result object and the function surface all changed; see
`MIGRATION.md`.

# Configuration

A version 2 registry declares species, their contigs and subgenomes, and one or
more assemblies. Contigs are paired by chromosome group; `group` is read from
the contig entry or from the first number in `name`.

```yaml
version: 2

defaults:
  windows_per_chromosome: 1000
  allowed_windows: [100, 1000, 10000]
  mapq: 20
  exclude_flags: 1796          # unmapped + secondary + QC-fail + duplicate
  metric: breadth              # breadth | count | combined
  score: paired_log_ratio      # paired_log_ratio | donor_only
  donor_aggregation: max       # mean | max | sum; default; Advanced panel
  mask:
    panel: null
    blacklist: null
    physical_fallback_mb: 1.0
    recurrence_threshold: 0.4
  calibration:
    length_bins_mb: [5, 10, 25, 50, 100, .inf]
    fdr: 0.01
    single_sample_floors: [2.0, 1.5, 1.2, 1.0, 0.5]

species:
  triticum_aestivum:
    label: "Triticum aestivum"
    gc_indexes: [/srv/mamamia/gcidx/triticum-aestivum/index.gcrank]
    contigs:
      - {id: CP155614.1, name: 1A, subgenome: A, group: 1}
      # ... 21 wheat contigs
  aegilops_speltoides:
    label: "Aegilops speltoides"
    gc_indexes: [/srv/mamamia/gcidx/aegilops-speltoides/index.gcrank]
    contigs:
      - {id: CH1S, name: 1S, subgenome: S, group: 1}
      # ... 7 S contigs

```

The registry declares species only. The donor and recipient are chosen at run
time and the assembly is derived from them:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pair <- resolveSpeciesAssembly(
    config,
    recipient = "triticum_aestivum",
    donor = "aegilops_speltoides",
    recipient_subgenomes = c("A", "B", "D"),
    donor_subgenomes = "S",
    default_sample_composition = c(A = 2, B = 2, D = 2)
)
```

`recipient_subgenome` and `donor_subgenome` are accepted as one-element
shortcuts. `copy_number` defaults to 2; `0` means absent. A runtime
`sample_composition` overrides `default_sample_composition`.

# Running the pipeline

```{r, eval = FALSE}
config <- readMaMaMIAConfig("assemblies.yml")
pair <- resolveSpeciesAssembly(
    config, donor = "aegilops_speltoides", recipient = "triticum_aestivum"
)
result <- analyzeBamInput(
    bam_paths, pair$config,
    assembly = pair$key,
    windows_per_chromosome = 1000L,
    cores = 8L
)
```

The bundled demo runs the same path:

```{r}
demo <- system.file("extdata", "bam-demo", package = "MaMaMIA")
config <- readMaMaMIAConfig(file.path(demo, "assemblies.yml"))
pair <- resolveSpeciesAssembly(
    config, donor = "secale_like", recipient = "triticum_like"
)
result <- analyzeBamInput(
    file.path(demo, "demo.bam"), pair$config,
    assembly = pair$key,
    windows_per_chromosome = 100L
)
names(result)
result$samples[, c("sample", "mode", "n_windows", "n_calls")]
```

# The result contract

`BamAnalysisResult` has eleven fields:

| Field | Contents |
|---|---|
| `assembly`, `config` | resolved assembly and validated registry |
| `bams`, `samples` | input metadata and per-sample call counts |
| `windows`, `gc` | exact-N windows and reference GC |
| `metrics` | one row per sample × window: count, covered, breadth, GC, lambdas |
| `scores` | one row per sample × group × window: score and residuals |
| `masks` | window-level mask with `source` and `version` |
| `calibration` | thresholds by mode and segment-length bin |
| `calls` | segments with class, confidence, method and `pass` |
| `provenance` | versions, parameters, mask/calibration hashes |

```{r}
head(result$metrics)
head(result$scores[, c("sample", "group", "iid", "score", "score_raw")])
result$calibration
```

# Ploidy and scoring

The primary score is

```
y = log(lambda_donor + eps) - log(lambda_recipient + eps)
```

where `lambda = -log(1 - breadth)` for `metric = "breadth"`. Recipient
homoeologs are averaged within a group. Donor homoeologs are max-selected by
default: at each window the donor subgenome with the strongest
donor/recipient log-ratio is used, so one strongly supported donor subgenome
is not diluted by the other donor homoeologs. `mean` and `sum` remain
available through the `donor_aggregation` setting; the registry supplies the
default and the dashboard exposes it in the **Advanced** sidebar panel. This
supports diploid, tetraploid, hexaploid and multi-donor designs. A single
sample is GC-corrected with a natural spline and centred; a cohort uses median
polish to remove the shared window effect and each sample's library/ploidy
offset.

`score = "donor_only"` is the CNV-robust fallback: it scores donor depth
without the recipient denominator.

# Masks and calibration

A mask is indexed by chromosome group and relative window. Sources are tried in
order: a fixed panel mask, a cohort recurrence mask (multi-sample), a BED
blacklist, and a physical terminal fallback. Masked windows are set to `NA`
before CBS, so segment boundaries and gap merging still see the full grid.

Calls are calibrated by segment length. The threshold is the empirical
`1 - fdr` quantile of control segment means, raised to a per-bin floor. A
single sample is its own control; a cohort uses all samples (or `controls`).

```{r}
result$calibration[, c("mode", "length_bin", "n_control", "threshold")]
```

# Export and dashboard

```{r, eval = FALSE}
writeCallsToBedpe(result, "calls.bedpe")
exploreIntrogressions(result)
```

`writeCallsToBedpe()` writes one row per passing call with donor and recipient
intervals, `score_mean`, `class`, `confidence`, `method` and `mode`.
`exploreIntrogressions()` opens the dashboard over every subgenome declared
for the species pair: chromosome-group, class, confidence and width filters, a
vertical karyotype with score-heatmap and call-map modes, a score profile with
called intervals, a call table, and a BEDPE export.
